cohort: 30 pregnant women at term (15 who received LEA and 15 who did not), excluding those with gestational age < 37 weeks, BMI ≥ 35 kg/m(2), cerebrovascular or cardiovascular complications, multiple pregnancies, gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes, chronic hypertension, thyroid disease, birth weight < 2,500 g, emergency cesarean section, or cases requiring re-administration of epidural anesthesia during delivery
finding: Maternal and fetal oxidative stress immediately after delivery was lower in the group who received labor epidural analgesia.
mod_finding: Mothers who received labor epidural analgesia (LEA) experienced less oxidative stress during childbirth compared to those who did not receive LEA.
